set -euo pipefail
cd /tmp
echo "== PySCF: H2 RHF/STO-3G, cross-checked against Psi4's value (recipe #20) =="
# Same molecule, method and basis as recipes/psi4 (#20), which reproduced -1.116783 Ha.
# PySCF is an independent integral/SCF stack, so this is a cross-code check -- the
# RAxML/IQ-TREE move in quantum chemistry. Note the agreement is BASIS-limited: STO-3G's
# contraction coefficients are not defined identically across packages, so two correct HF
# codes land ~2e-5 Ha apart (well inside chemical accuracy), not bit-identical.
python3 - <<'EOF' > smoke-check.txt || { cat smoke-check.txt; exit 1; }
import sys
from pyscf import gto, scf
mol = gto.M(atom="H 0 0 0; H 0 0 0.74", basis="sto-3g", unit="Angstrom", verbose=0)
mf = scf.RHF(mol); e = mf.kernel()
fail=[]
def check(l,ok,detail):
    print(f"{l:26s} {detail}")
    if not ok: fail.append(l)
check("scf_converged", bool(mf.converged), f"{mf.converged}  want True")
# PySCF's own reproducible value (pinned from a local run on this image)
check("pyscf_energy", abs(e-(-1.116759))<1e-4, f"{e:.6f} Ha  want -1.116759 +/-1e-4 (PySCF RHF/STO-3G)")
# cross-code: agrees with Psi4 (#20, -1.116783) to chemical accuracy. The gap is the
# STO-3G basis definition, not the SCF -- so the band is 1e-3 (1 mHa), not 1e-8.
delta=abs(e-(-1.116783))
check("cross_code_vs_psi4", delta<1e-3, f"|{e:.6f} - (-1.116783)| = {delta:.2e} < 1e-3 (Psi4 cross-check, basis-limited)")
# physical: below the H+H dissociation limit (2x -0.4666 Ha for H atom in STO-3G)
check("bound_state", e < -1.0, f"{e:.6f}  want < -1.0 (bound molecule)")
if fail: print("FAILED: "+", ".join(fail)); sys.exit(1)
EOF
cat smoke-check.txt
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
